title: Colour — the same parts
summary: Return to the familiar block and sphere, arranged with Transformation's positions and Arrays' indexed references. Build one five-part column and give each part its own material. A palette holds available colours; a second list assigns them to parts. Change the assignment, then the palette, while retaining every mesh and transform. Compose a grouping of separated parts and predict it before running. Carry a colour assignment that can change without rebuilding the body.
short: Same five parts. Palette = values; slots = destinations. Own materials. Reassign without remeshing. Predict a grouping.
change_note: The outline becomes the reviewed complete five-part program; the arrival from Arrays is explicit.
object: Five familiar mesh parts with separate materials and indexed colour assignments.
given: Prepared museum host, player, light; chosen part dimensions. One complete script creates the study.
check: Change an assignment and a palette value separately; object identity, geometry and transforms remain unchanged.
transfer: Make two separated parts share a colour while an intervening part differs; explain which list controls what.
carry: Palette values, assignment indices and independent material references.
next: Flashlight keeps the surface material and changes the light reaching it.
reflection: The reflection follows how colour gathers familiar parts into different apparent bodies.

title: Flashlight — keep the surface
summary: Encounter the installed grabbable lamps, then reconstruct their light-to-surface relation with a familiar box and two spotlights. Change one lamp's colour, then its aim, keeping the board and other lamp fixed. Use the local/world distinction when turning a light towards a local target. Choose a new target and predict which contribution moves. Carry the distinction between a material value and illumination; source edits provide controlled comparisons while the museum lamps supply the larger hand interaction.
short: Fixed board; two lights. Change one colour/aim. Local target → world look_at. Withdraw one contribution; material stays.
change_note: The guide becomes the reviewed complete light comparison, with its reduced scope declared.
object: One unchanged receiving board and two independent SpotLight3D nodes.
given: Museum light, player and installed lamp handles. The small study creates lights but no extra pickup handles.
check: Aim and light-colour edits preserve the board material and the second light; turned host preserves local targeting.
transfer: Choose another board target and predict the turn without attributing the result to repainting.
carry: Separate references for the light and the receiving material.
next: Nails uses the carried point to calculate a surface colour.
reflection: The reflection follows a contribution appearing and disappearing, then expands into the white room and apertures.

title: Nails — a position becomes a colour
summary: Bring back the same PointBody and its pickup behaviour. Express its position in the study's local frame, divide by the box dimensions, clamp the three channels and return a Color. Apply that result to a preview; the installed salon's hand bindings remain supplied. Choose a colour, work backwards to its position, and make a second independent receiver of the same returned value. Record one RGB triple for Rainbow. The handoff is an explicit copied value, not an automatic transfer between halls.
short: Inherited PointBody. Local p/size → clamp → Color → preview. Bound colour, not hand. Record RGB for Rainbow.
change_note: The operating guide becomes a complete continuation; both inherited classes are printed with it. VR pickup leads.
object: Inherited pickup point, three guides and a separate colour preview.
given: Prepared XR Tools; unchanged PointBody and LineSkin, both included. Salon distribution is outside this small reconstruction.
check: Each local axis changes its own RGB channel; moving the study preserves the mapping and out-of-range channels clamp.
transfer: Calculate a position for a chosen RGB triple and send the same returned value to a second independent material.
carry: A pure position-to-colour function and a recorded RGB choice.
next: Rainbow places that recorded choice among ordered bands.
reflection: The reflection asks what choosing nail colour and changing skin colour mean differently; that question is not reduced to the RGB calculation.

title: Rainbow — keep the opening
summary: Walk the celebration before choosing whether to make a small arch. Copy the recorded Nails colour into an ordered palette and divide a fixed radial thickness among its entries. Predict band width for two, three, four and one colour while the opening and outer radius stay fixed. The complete band builder is supplied from familiar mesh principles. Compose another palette and distinguish the number of colours from the number of parts: this example couples them, but that coupling is a choice. Carry the ordered palette without making coding a condition of joining the celebration.
short: Optional arch. Copy Nails RGB; palette length divides fixed thickness. Opening stays. Colour count need not equal part count.
change_note: The reviewed optional making lesson replaces the guide, including the full band builder and fixed-extent checks.
object: A small arch assembled from independently coloured semicircular bands.
given: Museum celebration and player; supplied, fully printed ArcStrip builder.
check: Every nonempty palette preserves inner and outer radii; adjoining bands meet and keep independent materials.
transfer: Choose a palette and predict band count, width and outer radius before running.
carry: An ordered palette and the distinction between available values and sampled parts.
next: Pillar replaces selection among entries with a position-to-colour function.
reflection: The reflection keeps the celebration open and asks who sets the divisions; the tutorial remains optional.

title: Pillar — colour has a height
summary: Return to the point and position-to-colour function, now through hue, saturation and value. Map a reachable hand-height range onto the tall museum field, then calculate colour separately. Keep X and Z fixed while moving Y; compare low, middle, high and out-of-range values. Choose another horizontal position and predict which HSV parameter changes. The existing pillars and ceiling illustrate the field; the study adds a sampler without rebuilding them. Record an RGB result for Grid, keeping HSV value distinct from illumination and perceived brightness.
short: Same point. Hand height → field height → HSV → RGB. Y controls V; no added light. Record sample for Grid.
change_note: The overview becomes the reviewed sampler program, with two coordinate mappings and the inherited point visible.
object: The returning PointBody with a carried preview and HSV/RGB readout.
given: Existing columns and ceiling; field dimensions are declared. Prepared pickup and original PointBody supplied.
check: Reachable low/high heights cover V=0/1; overshoot clamps; local-frame changes preserve the result.
transfer: Choose two positions with the same Y but different X or Z; predict the changed parameters.
carry: A recorded RGB sample and separate hand-to-field and field-to-colour functions.
next: Grid keeps a colour at an address after the sampler has moved.
reflection: The reflection follows the fog-like meeting of pillar and ceiling, and the difference between a field and its visible samples.

title: Grid — a colour left at an address
summary: Reuse Arrays' addresses and the recorded colours from Nails and Pillar in a compact grid. Introduce Palette as a small stateful class with an owned list and current index. Select an address, write one colour, then move elsewhere: the old tile keeps its value. Switch palettes without advancing the other instance, then apply a diagonal rule over all cells. The supplied museum pointer console calls these same operations. Compose a local arrangement and predict what the rule will overwrite. Carry independently owned state and distinguish cell address, instance index and palette index.
short: Two Palette instances. Select/write/advance separately. Address keeps colour. Rule overwrites; geometry stays. Pointer console supplied.
change_note: The fragment becomes four complete files. Labelled pointer controls replace keyboard-led instructions; the palette and grid operations remain the reviewed code.
object: A 5×5 addressed tile display and two independent Palette instances.
given: Prepared museum pointer; full GridSurface and labelled control implementation. No walking floor is created.
check: Stored colour survives selection changes; palette instances remain independent; actual pointer pressed events invoke the correct operations.
transfer: Paint a chosen arrangement, predict one cell's replacement under RULE, and distinguish its three indices.
carry: Palette class, owned state, explicit address binding and a retained colour per cell.
next: Paint retains deposits at finer surface addresses; Walls later reuses Palette unchanged.
reflection: The reflection asks what remains at a place after attention moves, and what a later rule overwrites.

title: Paint — a mark stays on the surface
summary: Keep PointBody's pickup and give it a named spray action. A held, active brush casts a ray; an accepted hit becomes a surface-local address and deposits colour into one retained image. First make a manual mark, miss the canvas, release and drop, checking that new deposits stop while previous ones remain. Change the radius or ink without changing targeting. The full receiver and support files are printed. An automatic caller is optional after this completion point: it uses the same receiver, rather than adding a second painting system. Carry a complete input-to-surface relation and identify where its result is stored.
short: Same PointBody. Held + spray + accepted ray → local UV → retained image. Miss/release/drop stop deposits. Automatic caller optional.
change_note: The guide becomes the reviewed complete manual-first reconstruction; preview instructions move out of the main interaction account.
object: Returning pickup point as a brush, one canvas and an accumulated image.
given: Prepared XR pickup/actions, unchanged PointBody, complete canvas and preview support. Aerosol, wetness and runs remain museum encounters.
check: Inactive, unheld, occluded and out-of-range inputs cannot deposit; valid hits accumulate; transformed surfaces keep the correct UV address.
transfer: Choose an ink and location, predict a mark, interrupt it, and identify the image retaining the result.
carry: Distinct action/hit states and one receiver usable by different callers.
next: Walls changes what a surface lets you see while retaining its physical boundary.
reflection: The reflection begins at an automatic painting already underway; the tutorial deliberately begins with the student's own accountable mark.

title: Walls — a view through two colours
summary: Bring back whole-body position and rotation and Grid's unchanged Palette class. Give two panes independent materials and palettes; change alpha and transparency mode together while retaining their colliders. Move to alter overlap, then change the second pane's turn to compose another view. The supplied pointer controls switch filter mode and advance the first palette. Arrange one view with overlap and another without, explaining which changes affect appearance and which affect passage. Carry independent source, placement and appearance choices into Tiling, where the familiar disco returns in colour.
short: Two panes; two Palettes. Alpha + render mode; collider stays. Move/view/turn separately. Carry independent palette into Pattern_Disco.
change_note: The guide becomes the complete two-pane composition. Supplied pointer targets provide the mode and colour controls.
object: Two transformed panes, separate materials, independent Palette instances and persistent colliders.
given: Prepared museum pointer and room; full pane construction and controls. Larger office and gradient models remain encounters.
check: Mode changes preserve RGB and collision; advancing the first palette leaves the second alone; pointer targets are ray-reachable.
transfer: Compose two viewpoints with different overlaps while preserving independent colour choices and solid boundaries.
carry: A composition separating source values, material state, placement, viewpoint and collision.
next: Pattern_Disco returns to the familiar pattern with an independently replaceable palette.
reflection: The reflection follows changing views through partitions and carries the unchanged-arrangement question into the coloured disco.
